assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain node of a knowledge-searcher meta-KB about where and how to find, retrieve, evaluate, and synthesize authoritative knowledge
target is RDF-based semantic web stack (RDF/RDFS/OWL/SPARQL/SHACL), not property-graph-only stacks
open-world OWL semantics and closed-world SHACL validation are treated as distinct mechanisms
exclusions: property-graph (LPG/Cypher/Gremlin) modeling as a primary stack
vector/embedding semantic search (covered by a sibling IR node)

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: at least one referenced object yields a decision for this question

competency_questions.question: Are resource and term IRIs stable, dereferenceable, and designed before publishing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: at least one referenced object yields a decision for this question

competency_questions.question: Does the RDF model correctly choose IRIs vs blank nodes vs typed literals for each value?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: at least one referenced object yields a decision for this question

competency_questions.question: Which standard vocabularies (FOAF, schema.org, Dublin Core, SKOS, PROV) cover each domain concept?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: at least one referenced object yields a decision for this question

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: at least one referenced object yields a decision for this question

glossary.definition: internationalized resource identifier naming an RDF resource
RDF node existentially scoped to a graph with no global identifier
RDF value with a datatype or language tag, never identified by an IRI
RDF Schema lightweight class/property vocabulary with inferential domain/range
tractable sublanguage of OWL 2 (EL, QL, RL) with bounded reasoning complexity
Shapes Constraint Language for closed-world RDF validation
SPARQL path expression for traversing predicate chains and closures
IRI-identified set of triples (a quad context) within a dataset
data published per the four principles: IRIs, HTTP dereference, RDF, outward links
assertion that two IRIs denote the same entity, merging all their statements
forward-chaining precomputation and storage of entailed triples
W3C provenance vocabulary for entities, activities, and agents

source_registry.description: model heuristic priors for semantic web and linked data design, scoring, conflict, and risk; no observed or benchmark dataset supplied
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Allemang & Hendler, Semantic Web for the Working Ontologist (2011); Staab & Studer, Handbook on Ontologies (2009)
grounding_limits: all scores are heuristic priors, not measured
no observed or experimentally validated labels permitted

nodes.definition: Define the knowledge-graph use case, source data, target queries, identity policy, and reuse-vs-build boundary before any RDF or ontology modeling.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: source data scope or query workload changes by >25%

pros.claim: Bounds vocabulary, profile, and store choices so downstream work targets real queries
pros.example: fix competency questions before choosing OWL EL vs RL

cons.claim: Premature scope lock can exclude later integration sources
cons.example: freezing identity policy before sameAs sources are known

failure_modes: scope omits a key query class
acceptance_tests: scope spec lists competency questions, sources, identity policy
reviewer confirms queries map to scope

nodes.definition: Design stable, dereferenceable IRI patterns (namespaces, slash vs hash, opacity, versioning) for resources and vocabulary terms.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: namespace authority or persistence policy changes

pros.claim: Stable dereferenceable IRIs are the foundation of link permanence and merge safety
pros.example: use w3id.org/PURL for persistent term IRIs

cons.claim: IRI scheme changes after publication break inbound links and cached data
cons.example: switching slash to hash after consumers cache triples

acceptance_tests: IRI doc fixes namespace, slash/hash, persistence owner
sample IRIs dereference to RDF descriptions

nodes.definition: Model the domain as RDF triples choosing IRIs vs blank nodes vs literals, datatypes, language tags, and reification/RDF-star for statement-level metadata.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: source schema or required statement-metadata changes

pros.claim: Correct triple/blank-node/literal choices keep data mergeable and queryable
pros.example: model author as IRI not literal so it links across graphs

cons.claim: Overusing blank nodes harms linkability and external reference
cons.example: skolemize needed to reference a blank node from outside

acceptance_tests: model spec names every literal datatype and blank-node use
sample data round-trips through Turtle and N-Triples

nodes.definition: Select and reuse standard vocabularies (FOAF, schema.org, Dublin Core, SKOS, PROV) before minting new terms, mapping domain concepts to existing terms.
outputs: gap list of terms to mint

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a better-fit standard vocabulary is published or deprecated

pros.claim: Reuse maximizes interoperability and reduces ontology maintenance burden
pros.example: use dcterms:created instead of a custom date property

cons.claim: Forcing a domain concept into an ill-fitting standard term distorts meaning
cons.example: misusing skos:broader for partonomy

failure_modes: misusing a term against its intended semantics
acceptance_tests: each domain concept mapped to reused or justified new term
no term duplicates a well-known standard term

nodes.definition: Define the RDFS layer: classes, properties, subClassOf/subPropertyOf hierarchies, domain and range, balancing expressivity against inference cost.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: class or property hierarchy needs restructuring for new queries

pros.claim: Lightweight RDFS gives useful subsumption and typing at low reasoning cost
pros.example: subPropertyOf lets one query cover specializations

cons.claim: RDFS domain/range are inferential not constraints and can mistype data
cons.example: rdfs:domain silently asserts a type, masking dirty data

acceptance_tests: hierarchy answers subsumption competency questions
domain/range documented as inferential not validation

nodes.definition: Choose an OWL profile (EL, QL, RL, or full DL) by matching required expressivity and reasoning tasks to each profile's tractability guarantees.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reasoning task or scale requires a different tractability class

pros.claim: Profile choice fixes whether reasoning is polynomial and which constructs are legal
pros.example: pick OWL RL for rule-based forward-chaining at scale

cons.claim: Wrong profile makes reasoning intractable or silently ignores axioms
cons.example: using qualified cardinality outside EL/RL breaks tractability

acceptance_tests: decision record maps reasoning tasks to a profile with rationale
all authored axioms validate inside the chosen profile

nodes.definition: Author OWL axioms (equivalences, disjointness, property characteristics, restrictions) within the chosen profile to encode intended entailments.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: intended entailments change or unintended entailments are found

pros.claim: Axioms let the reasoner derive facts and catch modeling contradictions
pros.example: disjointWith surfaces an instance asserted in two disjoint classes

cons.claim: Over-axiomatization causes surprising entailments and inconsistency under open-world
cons.example: careless owl:sameAs spreads wrong facts globally

acceptance_tests: each axiom traces to an intended entailment
reasoner reports no unintended inconsistency on sample data

nodes.definition: Author SHACL or ShEx shapes that express closed-world data constraints (cardinality, datatype, value sets, node shapes) distinct from OWL entailments.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: data quality requirements or RDF model shape changes

pros.claim: SHACL gives closed-world validation that OWL's open-world semantics cannot
pros.example: require exactly one foaf:mbox per Person via SHACL minCount/maxCount

cons.claim: Confusing SHACL constraints with OWL axioms yields wrong validation or inference
cons.example: expecting owl:cardinality to reject extra values

acceptance_tests: shapes encode each documented data constraint
sample valid and invalid data classify correctly

nodes.definition: Execute SHACL/ShEx validation over data, interpret validation reports, and gate ingestion on conformance.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: shapes change or new data source enters the pipeline

pros.claim: Validation gating keeps bad data out of the published graph
pros.example: block ingestion when a batch fails minCount on required keys

cons.claim: Blocking on noncritical violations stalls ingestion
cons.example: failing whole batch for one optional warning-level violation

acceptance_tests: validation report severity drives gate decision
nonconforming data quarantined not published

nodes.definition: Author SPARQL SELECT/ASK/CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE queries that answer competency questions with correct graph patterns, filters, and aggregation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: competency questions or schema shape changes

pros.claim: SPARQL directly answers competency questions and verifies model adequacy
pros.example: ASK query confirms every Person has a mappable label

cons.claim: Naive OPTIONAL/UNION patterns explode and return wrong cardinalities
cons.example: missing GROUP BY yields duplicated aggregate rows

acceptance_tests: each competency question has a passing query
query results match expected sample answers

nodes.definition: Use SPARQL property paths (sequence, alternative, transitive *, +) to traverse hierarchies and chains without explicit recursion.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: hierarchy depth grows or traversal queries time out

pros.claim: Property paths express transitive closure concisely over skos:broader or subClassOf
pros.example: one + path returns all ancestors of a concept

cons.claim: Unbounded transitive paths over large graphs are expensive and can time out
cons.example: * path over a dense graph scans millions of triples

failure_modes: path semantics misread for distinct results
acceptance_tests: path queries return expected transitive sets
path queries meet latency budget on sample data

nodes.definition: Author SPARQL Update (INSERT/DELETE/LOAD/CLEAR, INSERT-WHERE) to mutate graphs transactionally with idempotent, reversible operations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: mutation requirements or graph layout changes

pros.claim: INSERT-WHERE enables targeted, declarative graph edits without full reload
pros.example: delete superseded triples in one named graph atomically

cons.claim: Non-idempotent or unbounded DELETE WHERE can corrupt the graph irreversibly
cons.example: DELETE WHERE with a too-broad pattern wipes good data

acceptance_tests: updates are idempotent and have a rollback plan
destructive ops scoped to a named graph and reviewed

nodes.definition: Design federated SPARQL queries using SERVICE to join across remote endpoints, managing endpoint reliability, source selection, and result merging.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: remote endpoint availability or schema changes

pros.claim: Federation joins authoritative remote graphs without copying data
pros.example: SERVICE to Wikidata enriches local entities at query time

cons.claim: Remote endpoint latency or downtime makes federated queries fragile
cons.example: one slow SERVICE blocks the whole query

acceptance_tests: federated query degrades gracefully on endpoint failure
source selection avoids unnecessary remote calls

nodes.definition: Select a triple/quad store by matching scale, reasoning support, named-graph and SPARQL compliance, and operational profile to requirements.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: data scale or reasoning requirements outgrow the store

pros.claim: Right store matches reasoning mode and scale, avoiding costly later migration
pros.example: choose an RL-materializing store when forward-chaining is required

cons.claim: Store migration after data and queries exist is expensive and risky
cons.example: moving 1B triples and rewriting non-standard SPARQL extensions

failure_modes: store cannot scale to data volume
acceptance_tests: selection record maps requirements to store capabilities
SPARQL/SHACL/named-graph compliance verified on a proof load

nodes.definition: Decide and execute reasoning strategy: forward-chaining materialization vs backward-chaining at query time, and maintain inferred triples on data change.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ontology axioms change or inferred-data staleness detected

pros.claim: Materialization makes entailed facts queryable at low query-time cost
pros.example: precompute subClassOf closure so plain SPARQL sees inferred types

cons.claim: Materialized inferences go stale and must be re-derived on every data change
cons.example: forgetting to re-materialize after a delete leaves phantom inferences

acceptance_tests: strategy record states materialize vs query-time and refresh trigger
inferred graph re-derives correctly after a data change on sample

nodes.definition: Partition data into named graphs and attach provenance (PROV) so source, time, and trust of each statement set are tracked and queryable.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new source or trust/provenance requirement appears

pros.claim: Named graphs plus PROV let you query, update, and trust data per source
pros.example: drop and reload one source's named graph without touching others

cons.claim: Inconsistent graph granularity makes provenance queries and updates hard
cons.example: mixing two sources in one graph blocks per-source refresh

acceptance_tests: every asserted set has a named graph with PROV
per-source refresh and provenance queries succeed on sample

nodes.definition: Publish the graph as Linked Data following the four principles: dereferenceable IRIs, content negotiation, RDF descriptions, and outward links.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: IRI scheme, serialization support, or link targets change

pros.claim: Following the four principles makes data discoverable, dereferenceable, and linkable on the web
pros.example: content negotiation serves Turtle to agents and HTML to people

cons.claim: Publishing without stable IRIs or outward links yields a data silo, not Linked Data
cons.example: RDF dump with no dereference defeats web of data

acceptance_tests: sample IRIs dereference with content negotiation to RDF
graph has documented outward links and a VoID description

nodes.definition: Resolve and link entities to external datasets via owl:sameAs, skos:exactMatch, or weaker links, controlling identity-merge risk.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: external dataset changes or false-merge rate rises

pros.claim: Correct links enrich entities and integrate the graph into the wider web of data
pros.example: skos:exactMatch to a thesaurus aligns local and external concepts

cons.claim: A wrong owl:sameAs merges two real entities and propagates errors globally
cons.example: linking two distinct people as sameAs corrupts both records

acceptance_tests: sameAs links sampled and human-reviewed for false merges
weaker predicates used when identity is uncertain

nodes.definition: Assess and monitor knowledge-graph quality across accuracy, completeness, consistency, conciseness, and link validity dimensions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: quality scorecard regresses below threshold

pros.claim: Explicit quality dimensions turn vague trust into measurable, monitorable metrics
pros.example: track dead-link ratio and SHACL conformance over time

cons.claim: Optimizing one dimension (completeness) can hurt another (conciseness/consistency)
cons.example: mass-importing data raises completeness but adds dirty triples

failure_modes: quality measured but not acted on
acceptance_tests: scorecard covers accuracy, completeness, consistency, link validity
defects above threshold open backlog items

nodes.definition: Govern vocabulary and ontology evolution with versioning, deprecation, owl:deprecated, and change-impact analysis to protect downstream consumers.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a breaking ontology change is proposed

pros.claim: Versioning and deprecation let the vocabulary evolve without breaking consumers
pros.example: mark a term owl:deprecated and keep it resolvable for one cycle

cons.claim: Changing or removing a published term in place breaks all downstream data and queries
cons.example: deleting a property IRI invalidates consumer queries silently

failure_modes: breaking change with no version bump
acceptance_tests: breaking changes require version increment and impact report
deprecated terms remain resolvable for the deprecation window

edges.why_related: Scope and identity policy bound the IRI scheme
edges.example: competency questions decide which entities need stable IRIs
edges.resolution_rule: scope dominates; design IRIs to scope

edges.why_related: Scope and competency questions drive which vocabularies to reuse
edges.risk_of_conflict: vocab survey without scope is unfocused
edges.example: CQs about people pull in FOAF/schema.org

edges.why_related: IRI scheme constrains how resources are named in triples
Scope spec defines what entities and statements the RDF model must represent
edges.risk_of_conflict: modeling out of scope wastes effort

edges.why_related: Reused vocabularies supply many classes/properties the RDFS layer builds on
edges.example: extend schema:Person not a custom Person

edges.why_related: RDF triple shapes determine which classes and properties the RDFS layer formalizes
edges.example: property used in data gets domain/range

edges.why_related: Reused vocabularies' axioms constrain the achievable OWL profile
edges.example: importing a full-OWL vocab forces DL

edges.why_related: Schema expressivity needs drive profile selection
Profile fixes which axiom constructs are legal and tractable
RDF model shape defines what SHACL shapes must constrain
Schema classes/properties are the targets SHACL node and property shapes bind to
Shapes are the input the validation engine executes
Triple shapes determine the graph patterns queries must use
Property paths extend base SPARQL queries for traversal
edges.example: base query plus + path for ancestors

edges.why_related: Model shape defines what update operations may legally write
Named-graph layout scopes where updates write and delete
Local query patterns are the basis for federated SERVICE blocks
edges.risk_of_conflict: federation without local design is fragile

edges.why_related: Scale and workload from scope drive store selection
Chosen profile determines required reasoning support in the store
Axioms are the input the reasoner materializes or evaluates
Profile fixes the entailment regime and tractability of reasoning
Store capabilities determine materialize vs query-time reasoning options
Triple model plus source structure shape the named-graph partitioning
Dereferenceable IRIs are a precondition for Linked Data publishing
Only validated data should be published as Linked Data
The store hosts the endpoints that serve dereferenced descriptions
Materialized inferences should be settled before publishing dereferenceable data
Published, dereferenceable entities are the anchors external links point to
edges.example: sameAs targets a stable published IRI

edges.why_related: Reused linking predicates (owl:sameAs, skos:exactMatch) constrain link semantics
Validation reports feed the quality scorecard
Link validity and false-merge rate are quality dimensions
Richer axioms increase entailments but raise reasoning cost and inconsistency risk
edges.resolution_rule: keep axioms within profile budget; drop low-value axioms

edges.why_related: OWL open-world entailment and SHACL closed-world validation pull modeling in opposite directions
edges.resolution_rule: use OWL for inference, SHACL for validation

edges.why_related: Publishing stable IRIs conflicts with the need to evolve the vocabulary
edges.example: renaming a published property breaks queries
edges.resolution_rule: versioning and deprecation dominate; never mutate in place

edges.why_related: Federated remote dependence conflicts with self-contained, reliable publishing
edges.example: SERVICE failure empties a published view
edges.resolution_rule: prefer cached/materialized for published critical views

edges.why_related: Aggressive linking raises completeness but risks false merges hurting accuracy
edges.resolution_rule: accuracy dominates; require review for sameAs

edges.why_related: Quality findings can trigger rescoping of sources or competency questions
edges.resolution_rule: stop when scorecard meets threshold; max one rescope per cycle

edges.why_related: Persistent validation failures can trigger RDF model revision
edges.example: repeated minCount fails reveal a missing property
edges.resolution_rule: revise model only on error-severity; max two revisions per cycle

edges.why_related: Unintended entailments from reasoning trigger axiom revision
edges.example: reasoner flags inconsistency from a bad disjointness
edges.resolution_rule: revise axioms until reasoner consistent; max three passes

edges.why_related: Transitive property paths and materialized closure both compute reachability over hierarchies
edges.risk_of_conflict: confusing query-time paths with materialized inference
edges.resolution_rule: choose paths for ad-hoc, materialization for hot queries

conflict_axes.trigger: open-world OWL entailment is used where closed-world SHACL validation is needed
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: OWL infers; SHACL validates. Constraints go in SHACL, entailments in OWL.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: missing-required-property treated as inference not violation
conflict_axes.example: team uses owl:cardinality to reject extra values

conflict_axes.trigger: desired axioms exceed the tractable profile or reasoning budget
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: tractability dominates; keep axioms within the chosen profile and drop low-value ones
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: qualified cardinality requested in OWL EL
conflict_axes.example: reasoning exceeds latency budget after adding restrictions

conflict_axes.trigger: a standard term almost-but-not-quite fits a domain concept
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: reuse dominates unless semantic mismatch is material; then mint a documented subterm

conflict_axes.trigger: evolving the vocabulary would change or remove published IRIs
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: stability dominates published IRIs; evolve via versioning and deprecation, never in place
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: deleting a term still referenced by external data
conflict_axes.example: renaming a published property breaks consumer queries

conflict_axes.trigger: aggressive sameAs linking raises completeness but risks false merges
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: accuracy dominates; require review or weaker predicates when identity is uncertain
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: bulk import adds many low-confidence links
conflict_axes.example: auto-sameAs on name match merges two people

conflict_axes.trigger: live remote SERVICE dependence threatens reliability of published views
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: reliability dominates published critical views; cache or materialize remote data
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: slow SERVICE blocks the whole query
conflict_axes.example: remote endpoint outage empties a served page

conflict_axes.trigger: inference can be precomputed or evaluated at query time with different cost/staleness tradeoffs
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: materialize hot, stable entailments; evaluate volatile ones at query time
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: path query recomputes closure every call
conflict_axes.example: subClassOf closure materialized but goes stale after delete

conflict_axes.trigger: modeling a value as a blank node blocks external linking and reference
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: mint IRIs for anything that must be referenced or linked; reserve blank nodes for truly local structure
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: skolemization needed to reference a bnode
conflict_axes.example: address as blank node cannot be linked across graphs

conflict_axes.trigger: fine-grained named graphs aid provenance/refresh but add management overhead
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: granularity follows refresh and provenance boundaries; avoid per-triple graphs
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: too many tiny graphs slow management

edge_cases.trigger: OWL cardinality/restriction used to reject data
edge_cases.failure_mode: open-world axiom never flags the violation it was meant to catch
edge_cases.example: owl:maxCardinality 1 fails to reject a second value
edge_cases.detection_method: compare expected SHACL violations against OWL entailments on test data

edge_cases.failure_mode: wrong global merge propagates incorrect facts across graphs
edge_cases.example: two different people merged by name match
edge_cases.detection_method: sample sameAs links and check for conflicting attributes (e.g. two birthdates)

edge_cases.trigger: published IRI returns no RDF on dereference
edge_cases.failure_mode: data fails the Linked Data principles and is a silo
edge_cases.example: 404 or HTML-only response for a resource IRI
edge_cases.detection_method: crawl sample IRIs and assert RDF returned under content negotiation

edge_cases.trigger: transitive * path over a dense large graph
edge_cases.failure_mode: query times out or exhausts memory
edge_cases.detection_method: run path queries against scaled sample with a timeout budget

edge_cases.example: DELETE WHERE {?s ?p ?o} run on wrong endpoint
edge_cases.detection_method: require dry-run count and named-graph scope before destructive ops

edge_cases.trigger: data changed but inferred triples not re-derived
edge_cases.failure_mode: queries return phantom or missing inferences
edge_cases.example: deleted instance still has inferred type in store
edge_cases.detection_method: checksum or timestamp inferred graph against base data change log

edge_cases.trigger: remote SERVICE endpoint slow or down
edge_cases.failure_mode: federated query hangs or returns silent partial results
edge_cases.example: one SERVICE block blocks the entire query
edge_cases.detection_method: inject endpoint failure in test and assert graceful degradation
resolution: mark optional and fall back to cache

edge_cases.trigger: data uses a deprecated term while consumers expect the new one
edge_cases.failure_mode: queries silently miss data across versions
edge_cases.example: old property IRI coexists with renamed one
edge_cases.detection_method: audit data for deprecated IRIs after a version bump

edge_cases.trigger: externally-referenceable entity modeled as blank node
edge_cases.failure_mode: cannot be linked, merged, or dereferenced by consumers
edge_cases.example: an organization left as a blank node
edge_cases.detection_method: scan published graph for blank nodes in subject position of key classes

edge_cases.trigger: asserted facts have no named graph or PROV metadata
edge_cases.failure_mode: trust, audit, and per-source refresh impossible
edge_cases.example: facts loaded into default graph with no source tag
edge_cases.detection_method: query for triples whose graph lacks a PROV activity

edge_cases.trigger: rdfs:domain/range treated as a constraint that rejects data
edge_cases.failure_mode: dirty data silently retyped instead of flagged
edge_cases.example: rdfs:domain infers a wrong type rather than erroring
edge_cases.detection_method: compare RDFS inference results with SHACL validation on dirty samples

workflow.objective: Fix use case, sources, competency questions, identity policy
acceptance_tests: scope spec lists CQs, sources, identity policy
exit_criteria: scope reviewed and frozen for draft
workflow.do_first_because: scope bounds every downstream vocabulary, profile, and store choice (highest coupling foundation)

workflow.objective: Design stable dereferenceable IRI scheme and namespaces
acceptance_tests: IRI doc fixes namespace, slash/hash, persistence owner
workflow.do_first_because: IRI scheme is irreversible once published, so fix it before modeling and publishing

workflow.objective: Survey and select standard vocabularies; decide reuse vs mint
acceptance_tests: each concept mapped to reused or justified new term
workflow.do_first_because: reuse decisions must precede schema and axiom authoring to avoid reinventing terms

workflow.objective: Model triples and the RDFS class/property layer
acceptance_tests: model names each literal datatype and blank-node use
hierarchy answers subsumption CQs
workflow.do_first_because: model and schema are the substrate for axioms, shapes, and queries

workflow.objective: Select OWL profile and author in-profile axioms
acceptance_tests: axioms validate inside chosen profile
each axiom traces to an intended entailment
workflow.do_first_because: profile choice is high-irreversibility and constrains axioms, reasoning, and store

workflow.objective: Author SHACL/ShEx shapes and run validation gating
acceptance_tests: shapes encode each documented constraint
sample valid/invalid data classify correctly
workflow.do_first_because: validation must gate data before publishing to keep the published graph clean

workflow.objective: Select store and decide reasoning materialization strategy
acceptance_tests: compliance verified on proof load
inferred graph re-derives after data change on sample
workflow.do_first_because: store and reasoning choices are high-irreversibility and must pass before publishing

workflow.objective: Define named-graph layout, PROV, and safe update operations
acceptance_tests: every asserted set has a named graph with PROV
updates idempotent with rollback plan
workflow.do_first_because: provenance partitioning enables safe per-source updates and trust before publishing

workflow.objective: Publish Linked Data and validate query coverage
acceptance_tests: sample IRIs dereference under content negotiation
each CQ has a passing query
exit_criteria: endpoints live and query coverage met
workflow.do_first_because: publishing exposes irreversible IRIs and must follow validation and infrastructure gates

workflow.objective: Link entities, assess quality, and govern change
acceptance_tests: sameAs links sampled and human-reviewed
scorecard covers core dimensions
breaking changes require version increment
exit_criteria: quality threshold met and change control in place
workflow.do_first_because: linking, quality, and versioning run continuously after publish and feed rescoping

dominance_rules.trigger: high risk_if_wrong conflicts with shipping speed
dominance_rules.rule: block release when a high-risk node lacks passing acceptance tests
dominance_rules.example: do not publish sameAs links without human review

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is ordered before its unmet prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: respect dependency precedence over raw importance
dominance_rules.example: publish only after validation and store selection pass

dominance_rules.trigger: numeric precision is presented as certainty beyond evidence
dominance_rules.rule: keep heuristic labels; do not imply observed accuracy
dominance_rules.required_action: label all estimates heuristic until data exists
dominance_rules.example: no observed performance numbers without a measured source

dominance_rules.trigger: an artifact is proposed for lock before QA passes
dominance_rules.rule: no soft/hard lock before validation and acceptance tests pass
dominance_rules.required_action: run validation before any lock upgrade
dominance_rules.example: do not soft-lock published endpoints before query coverage met

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or high-risk action is about to run automatically
dominance_rules.rule: require human review for irreversible or high-risk operations
dominance_rules.required_action: route to human reviewer before executing
dominance_rules.example: human signs off destructive SPARQL Update

dominance_rules.trigger: adding more terms/data destabilizes the schema
dominance_rules.rule: stabilize schema and IRI scheme before mass population

dominance_rules.trigger: output formatting tempts prose or markdown in the artifact
dominance_rules.rule: strict JSON dominates prose quality in all artifacts
dominance_rules.example: KB file stays valid JSON, no comments

dominance_rules.trigger: a claim lacks a resolvable source
dominance_rules.rule: every claim cites a registered source or is downgraded
dominance_rules.example: no benchmark claim without a source record

dominance_rules.trigger: a locally optimal step would force later rework
dominance_rules.required_action: follow the workflow order, defer premature optimization
dominance_rules.example: do not optimize SPARQL before model is stable

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient ordering would introduce a dependency cycle
dominance_rules.rule: dependency graph must stay acyclic; convert weaker links to sequence/feedback
dominance_rules.required_action: split node or downgrade edge to break the cycle
dominance_rules.example: reasoning->axiom revision is feedback not dependency

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve inputs and identity policy before locking scope
anti_rework_rules.rationale: scope built on missing inputs gets reopened
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: scope frozen while sources still unknown
anti_rework_rules.example: freezing scope before source inventory exists

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix competency questions before populating schema or shapes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: schema without CQs models the wrong things
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: classes added with no driving query
anti_rework_rules.example: building a class hierarchy with no query needing it

anti_rework_rules.rule: survey standard vocabularies before minting new terms
anti_rework_rules.rationale: minting duplicates of standard terms forces later migration
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: new term duplicates dcterms or foaf
anti_rework_rules.example: creating a custom name property instead of foaf:name

anti_rework_rules.rule: finalize the IRI scheme before publishing any dereferenceable data
anti_rework_rules.rationale: changing IRIs after publish breaks all inbound links
anti_rework_rules.example: switching slash/hash after consumers cache data

anti_rework_rules.rule: stabilize the RDF model before authoring SHACL shapes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: shapes authored against a moving model thrash
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: shapes target predicates that get renamed
anti_rework_rules.example: writing shapes before datatype map is fixed

anti_rework_rules.rule: choose the OWL profile before authoring axioms
anti_rework_rules.rationale: axioms outside the profile must be rewritten or dropped
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: author qualified cardinality then switch to EL
anti_rework_rules.example: writing DL axioms before deciding on EL/QL/RL

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate data before publishing it as Linked Data
anti_rework_rules.rationale: publishing bad data forces public retraction

anti_rework_rules.rule: select store and reasoning strategy before publishing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: store migration after publish is costly and risky
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: publish then find store cannot scale
anti_rework_rules.example: serving from a store that lacks named-graph support

anti_rework_rules.rule: define named-graph layout before running updates
anti_rework_rules.rationale: unscoped updates corrupt or lose data
anti_rework_rules.example: mutating the default graph mixing all sources

anti_rework_rules.rule: run change-control before any breaking vocabulary change
anti_rework_rules.rationale: in-place breaking changes silently break consumers
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: remove a published property with no version bump
anti_rework_rules.example: deleting a term still used by external data

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or eval reports a failure
acceptance_tests: all failures enumerated

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and dependency depth
action: order by risk and blast radius
acceptance_tests: high-risk defects ranked first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only low-risk warnings remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling or locked node
acceptance_tests: impact set lists all affected objects
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set stable across a pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is assigned for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to repair subsystem
action: apply fix via formula script or reference fix
acceptance_tests: each defect routed to an owner
no new failures introduced
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: validation passes or no material delta

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence or failure-rate signal appears
action: recompute PI*EC (or observed formula if data)
acceptance_tests: posterior recomputed within tolerance

iteration_protocol.trigger: a dependency cycle or mislabeled edge is found
acceptance_tests: dependency graph acyclic
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no cycle and no mislabeled edges

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream dependency changed under a locked node
iteration_protocol.detection: detect upstream change vs lock state
acceptance_tests: affected locks downgraded
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no locked artifact has unreviewed upstream change

iteration_protocol.trigger: risk>=0.80 or confidence<0.65 or irreversible action
acceptance_tests: high-risk items have a decision record

test_cases.input_summary: single small KG with one source and a few competency questions
published Linked Data enriched by a remote endpoint

lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade from soft_lock if upstream dependency changes
downgrade on posterior delta above threshold
